# Background information

This is how the FIPS provider and it's enclosing libctx look:

![Pauli CAD Productions Present](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/assets/17916609/a4b7ff4f-efda-4c91-85b3-abcca70056d4)

The entropy/nonce up calls take an OSSL_CORE_HANDLE pointer as their first argument.  The problem is that the existing validated FIPS providers are passing a pointer to their internal core handle, what is required is a pointer to the external core handle.  From the outside (libcrypto), it isn't possible to inspect the structures internal to the FIPS provider and navigate the pointers correctly because we've no idea of their internal structure because they are opaque.

* Fortunately, a newer provider passing a different pointer to an older libcrypto, isn't a problem.  The underlying implementation of these up-calls in an older libcrypo implementation doesn't use the passed pointer.
* The problem is supporting an older FIPS provider with a newer libcrypto.  The older FIPS providers are passing a pointer that is _completely useless_, so libcrypo will have no idea what libctx is being used.  At the time the decision needs to be made as to old or new, there is no context to provide an answer.

I see three possible options moving forwards:
1. Accept that we've got a breaking change, fix it in 4.0 with a statement that 4.0 is not compatible with 3.x FIPS providers.
2. Determine if the FIPS provider being used is savvy or not and store this information in a thread local global.  Retrieve the global when called on to figure out what to do.  The global cannot even be tied to a libctx because that information isn't available.
3. Introduce new up-calls that do the same thing.  An old provider will always call the old up-calls, a new provider the new ones if they exist and the old ones if not.  The new up-calls would essentially look like duplicates of the existing ones.

Thanks for the picture! It explains the problem very nicely.

IMO clearly the option (3) is the right way as (2) seems to me like a terrible hack and (1) is bad as we AFAIK did not want to break the backward compatibility of providers on 4.0.

issue_context.title: Unable to set entropy seed source for FIPS provider
issue_context.body:
Currently it is possible to replace libcrypto's entropy seed source and libcrypto will use what is specified.

Normally the FIPS provider calls back to libcrypto for its seeding material, however this doesn't use the instantiated seed source.  Instead it calls direct into OpenSSL's own entropy gathering code.  It shouldn't.

`ossl_rand_get_entropy` in `crypto/rand/prov_seed.c` needs updating for both entropy and nonce input.
comments: This looks to be quite ugly.  The seed source needs to be instantiated before loading the FIPS provider because it is used during the self test phase which is on module load and before the provider start/initialisation call.  Not having it setup leads to a recursive lock in a very deep call chain.
Could you start with some default seed source and replace it later? Especially because we have to fix the RNG during the self-test so the KATs are possible for DSA/ECDSA and others.

We fire up a different RNG and don't involve the DRBGs for the DSA/ECDSA KATs.  They aren't a problem.

The seed source needs to be inserted in two places -- in the FIPS provider's internal libctx and in the one where the FIPS provider was loaded.

Changing the seed source would require rerunning the CRNG tests and forcing a reseeding.  I tried doing this and it's possible but when/where to force the reseeding is problematic.

My current thought is to cerate the RNG seed source as part of the initialisation code, that's early enough to ensure it's used.  It's not a heavy object, so the overhead if it isn't used is not large.
